name: Delphi (Digital Mind)
what: Creators build a chatbot 'digital mind' from their books, articles, podcasts, YouTube and courses; hosted free and paid tiers, REST API top tier only.
why_it_matters: Closest commercial analogue to a person-as-advisor; the cited-answer claim is from third-party reviews, not the product page.
numbers: Pricing conflicts across third-party sources: $79/mo creators and $299/mo leaders (startupsignals substack); creator plans from ~$19 (tooldirectory.ai) or $29 (other directory); Matthew Hussey clone $39/mo. Source: https://startupsignals.substack.com/p/delphi-can-you-package-a-mind
note: grounding: creator corpus RAG (claimed); cites: claimed by reviews only; refuses: not verified; consent: creator self-serve, terms not read

name: Dexa (Huberman AI search)
what: AI search over podcast transcripts; returns an AI summary plus pointers to episodes and timestamped links; began as Huberman-focused tool, now multi-podcast.
why_it_matters: Best live example of a summary-with-timestamped-source UI on one person's catalogue; shows citation-by-link but no published refusal rule.
numbers: 120+ podcasts indexed (TechCrunch, 5 Feb 2024); $6M seed (BetaKit); no revenue then, subscriptions and ads considered. Source: https://techcrunch.com/2024/02/05/dexa-aims-to-get-more-out-of-podcasts-with-ai-powered-search
note: grounding: transcript search + summary; cites: yes, timestamped episode links; refuses: not stated; consent: Huberman Lab partnership, free access for listeners

name: Character.AI (celebrity and likeness bots)
what: Hosts user-made bots of real figures (e.g. Nicki Minaj, Elon Musk, Donald Trump per search coverage); removals happen after complaints, rightsholder letters or press inquiries, not proactive.
why_it_matters: Shows the default for person bots is complaint-driven takedown; the stated impersonation clause could not be re-verified.
numbers: Garcia and four other teen-harm suits settled Jan 2026, terms undisclosed (citizen.digital). Disney C&D removals were partial (NBC News).
note: grounding: none (roleplay); cites: no; refuses: no; consent: no published public-figure permission process found; ConductAtlas says impersonation clause no longer published, correction CR-002704 flags it unverifiable

name: Meta AI celebrity personas (discontinued)
what: Celebrity-licensed chat personas (Snoop Dogg, Tom Brady, Kendall Jenner); played archetypes, not the celebrity's own voice or record; shut down or de-celebritied within about a year.
why_it_matters: Failure case for celebrity likeness deals: low engagement despite fees; a benchmark for why a person-advisor needs a grounded corpus, not a persona.
numbers: Reported up to $5M per celebrity likeness fee and low follower uptake (Digital Trends, TechRadar; press reports, not Meta disclosures).
note: grounding: persona prompt; cites: no; refuses: no; consent: licensed likeness fees

name: Hello History
what: One-on-one chats with AI-generated historical figures; app store product; no citation feature and no accuracy disclaimer on the research page.
why_it_matters: Contrast case: persona chat for dead figures with no disclosed sourcing; not a corpus-grounded advisor.
numbers: Subscription $2 to $35/month, free tier (topai.tools listing, unverified against store). Source: https://topai.tools/s/history-ai
note: grounding: none disclosed; cites: no; refuses: no; consent: n/a (historical figures)

name: Essays by Paul Graham GPT (third-party custom GPT)
what: Third-party custom GPT that answers only from paulgraham.com essays and cites them; built because GPT was guessing what PG would say. Not official.
why_it_matters: Closest public match to our spec (corpus-only plus cites), but reliance on the model's answer discipline is untested.
numbers: Corpus size disputed: 1200+ pages / 500k words vs curated 200+ essays (listings, aipure.ai and productcool). Requires ChatGPT Plus per listing.
note: grounding: essay RAG (custom GPT); cites: claimed yes; refuses: not verified; consent: author not involved (public essays)

name: Ask Naval / Naval AI (fan bots)
what: Fan-made bots not affiliated with Naval Ravikant; trained on tweets, interviews and The Almanack of Naval Ravikant (Eric Jorgenson); answers in his style.
why_it_matters: Shows the default for popular advisors: mixed corpus, style-mimicry, no disclosed citations, no author endorsement.
numbers: No pricing or usage numbers found in listings (creati.ai, toolify, logicweb).
note: grounding: mixed corpus plus model; cites: no; refuses: no; consent: none, unaffiliated

name: StoryFile (interactive oral history)
what: Subject records answers to many pre-scripted questions; visitors ask questions and the system retrieves a matching clip. It never generates new speech. Museum deployments include Holocaust survivor testimony.
why_it_matters: The strongest existing pattern for quote-only fidelity: retrieval over recorded verbatim answers, with a fallback to the closest recorded question and operator override.
numbers: One museum estimate about $250,000 per subject (recording, interface, education) (press coverage, 2023 era). Matching errors were seen at live events.
note: grounding: pre-recorded answers retrieved, no generation; cites: clip-level; refuses: redirects to closest question; consent: subject records own answers

name: HereAfter AI
what: Person records life stories with the company before death; family can then talk to an avatar built from those recordings. Subject signs an agreement before death.
why_it_matters: Clearest opt-in model for a post-mortem advisor: consent captured from the subject while alive.
numbers: Plans from USD 39 per year (2022 commentary). Current terms not checked.
note: grounding: subject's own recordings; cites: not found; refuses: not found; consent: subject signs pre-death agreement

name: Rai 1 Ipazia (AI avatar on Codice)
what: AI avatar on Rai 1's Codice that answers live over a retrieval system on the show's archive. It is a fictional branded avatar named after Hypatia, not a real person.
why_it_matters: Broadcaster pattern: archive RAG with on-air answers; a template for a corpus-bounded advisor on TV.
numbers: Debut episode 4 Sep 2026; RAG over about a decade of archive (single blog source, no Rai release found).
note: grounding: archive RAG (claimed); cites: not stated; refuses: not stated; consent: not a real person

name: ElevenLabs Iconic Marketplace
what: Marketplace where licensed celebrity voices (e.g. Michael Caine, Matthew McConaughey as investor) are approved for brand use; rights holders approve each script.
why_it_matters: Live model of opt-in, per-use consent for a living person's likeness with approval rights; relevant to any advisor that uses a real voice.
numbers: Script review within average 72 hours (company announcement, Nov 2025); no license fee published (press); terms set per deal.
note: grounding: voice model, no corpus Q&A; cites: no; refuses: approval gate; consent: opt-in license, per-use approval, negotiated terms

name: Sensay (digital replicas)
what: London startup making 'replicas' trained on a person's documents, video, interviews and email; has a hallucination warning flag on answers that rely on assumed information; proof-of-humanity link.
why_it_matters: Only product found with an explicit per-answer 'not from source' flag, which is half of our refusal rule.
numbers: Founder claim 90% to 95% indistinguishable (Thomson, unverified). NFT minting per replica (press release).
note: grounding: multi-source persona RAG; cites: hallucination flag not citations; refuses: flags assumed content; consent: proof-of-humanity

name: Personal.ai
what: Personal memory and digital twin that stores a user's messages, notes and documents as memory stacks.
why_it_matters: Pricing and memory model for a self-owned advisor; no evidence found of answer-only-from-data or per-answer citations.
numbers: Individual $40/mo or $400/yr, 50k memory cap, 10k messages; enterprise from $1,000/mo (undated pricing snapshot via search summary, verify). Source: https://www.personal.ai/insights
note: grounding: personal memory store; cites: not found; refuses: not found; consent: owner controls own data (company claim)

name: Amazon Kindle Ask This Book
what: Always-on AI Q&A inside Kindle books, live on some devices since Dec 2025; publishers and authors cannot opt out.
why_it_matters: Live example of an author's book answering questions with no consent gate; the Authors Guild dispute is the consent precedent for any book-based advisor.
numbers: No opt-out (Amazon spokesperson via Writer Beware, Dec 2025). Authors Guild statement is primary.
note: grounding: book text RAG; cites: not confirmed; refuses: not confirmed; consent: none, no opt-out

name: BBC Maestro Agatha Christie Writing (AI version)
what: Online writing course taught by an AI version of Christie built from her texts and interviews, approved by the estate; criticised for consent of the dead.
why_it_matters: Estate-approved post-mortem persona; shows estate sign-off does not settle the ethics objection.
numbers: Price $89 (NYT via press). Course is about 2.5 hours (Killzone blog).
note: grounding: estate texts (paraphrase disputed); cites: no; refuses: no; consent: estate approval, Veliz says the dead cannot consent

name: Replika / Luka Inc. Garante fine (incident)
what: Italy's data authority fined Luka Inc. EUR 5 million for no valid legal basis, a privacy notice that did not explain purposes or rights, and weak age checks.
why_it_matters: Regulatory precedent for companion or persona bots under GDPR: legal basis and minors, not likeness.
numbers: EUR 5M fine announced 19 May 2025 (press); earlier processing limit Feb 2023.
note: grounding: n/a; cites: n/a; refuses: n/a; consent: GDPR legal basis and age gate, not emotional consent

name: NPR: AI deadbots, Parkland case
what: Overview of AI deadbots of dead people, including a Parkland shooting victim's likeness used in court; researchers warn deadbots are primed for monetisation and persuasion.
why_it_matters: Incident evidence that deadbots are used in legal and public settings without the subject's consent.
numbers: Only search snippet read (fetch timed out); no figures used.
note: grounding: n/a; cites: n/a; refuses: n/a; consent: none for the dead

name: Generative Agent Simulations of 1,000 People (Park et al.)
what: Agents grounded in 2-hour qualitative interviews of 1,052 Americans, scored on held-out GSS, personality and economic-game answers.
why_it_matters: Best evidence that an interview-grounded persona tracks a real person; the paper does not test refusal or citation.
numbers: Normalized accuracy vs participants own 2-week retest: interview-only 83%, survey-only 82%, combined 86%, demographics-only 74% (arXiv abstract page, v3 28 Jun 2026).
note: grounding: interview transcript in prompt; cites: no; refuses: not tested; consent: participants consented to research; HAI flags privacy and misuse | check: arXiv 2411.10109 v3 (28 Jun 2026): 1,052 Americans; interview-only 83%, survey-only 82%, combined 86%, demographics-only 74%, all relative to participants' own 2-week retest. Abstract does not use the phrase 'normalized accuracy'.

name: ALCE: Enabling LLMs to Generate Text with Citations (Gao et al., EMNLP 2023)
what: First benchmark for citation evaluation (ASQA, QAMPARI, ELI5); scores fluency, correctness and citation quality.
why_it_matters: Standard metric for our cite-every-sentence rule; the citation-recall definition is what we should copy.
numbers: On ELI5 the best models lack complete citation support about 50% of the time (version-dependent: 49 generations in v1 abstract). Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14627
note: grounding: retrieval then cited generation; cites: metric; refuses: not in scope; consent: n/a | check: arXiv 2305.14627 abstract: on ELI5 'even the best models lack complete citation support 50% of the time'. Matches. The '49 generations in v1' detail was not visible on the abstract page.

name: TwinVoice (benchmark for LLM digital twins of specific people)
what: Benchmark for whether LLMs can act as convincing digital twins of specific people; scores mindset coherence and linguistic expression.
why_it_matters: Only persona-to-real-person benchmark found; can measure how our advisor matches a person's voice.
numbers: No figures read. arXiv ID not confirmed (aggregator cites Du et al., 29 Oct 2025).
note: grounding: n/a; cites: n/a; refuses: n/a; consent: n/a; primary paper not located

name: Quantifying and Optimizing Global Faithfulness in Persona-driven Role-playing (Peng and Shang)
what: Quantifies how faithful a role-play LLM is to a persona document and proposes a fine-grained faithfulness score.
why_it_matters: Metric for checking an answer stays inside the persona document; adaptable to a corpus.
numbers: No figures read in this pass.
note: grounding: persona doc; cites: no; refuses: no; consent: n/a

name: PersonaEval (who is speaking benchmark)
what: Tests whether LLM judges can identify which character is speaking, using novel, script and transcript dialogue.
why_it_matters: Shows models stay weak at telling a person apart from the persona; a check for our voice-fidelity eval.
numbers: Best LLMs about 69% accuracy vs about 90.8% for humans (per summary; verify in paper).
note: grounding: n/a; cites: n/a; refuses: n/a; consent: n/a; dialogue is fictional, not public statements

name: NO FAKES Act (S.1367 / H.R.2794)
what: Federal bill creating a property right in voice and visual likeness, with notice-and-takedown duties for platforms and a post-mortem right up to 70 years.
why_it_matters: Would govern any living or dead person's replica used in an advisor; still pending as of last search.
numbers: Reintroduced 9 Apr 2025 (Blackburn, Coons, Tillis, Klobuchar; Salazar, Dean). Post-mortem up to 70 years (Baker Botts, Regulatory Review). Status: committee.
note: law: federal likeness right, pending; platform liability on knowledge; state preemption carve-outs | check: Reintroduced April 2025 as S.1367 / H.R.2794 (Regulatory Review); post-mortem 'more than 70 years' for commercial use; still in committee and no later action found (congress.gov and govtrack returned 403/blocked).

name: Tennessee ELVIS Act
what: Adds voice to Tennessee's Personal Rights Protection Act; creates liability for tools whose primary purpose is unauthorised voice or likeness facsimiles.
why_it_matters: Only enacted US state law that reaches the voice and the tool maker; relevant to any voice-based advisor sold into Tennessee.
numbers: Signed 21 Mar 2024, effective 1 Jul 2024; misdemeanor plus private action; treble damages if knowing. Statute Tenn. Code Ann. 47-25-1101 et seq. (verify text).
note: law: voice right of publicity; tool liability; in force | check: Signed 21 Mar 2024 and effective 1 Jul 2024 confirmed (WSGR/Proskauer), private cause of action against tool distributors confirmed. Treble damages for knowing violations NOT found in fetched sources; remove or source it.

name: EU AI Act Article 50 (transparency duties)
what: Chatbot disclosure (50(1)) and deepfake disclosure (50(4)) apply from 2 Aug 2026; AI-generated public-interest text needs disclosure; machine-readable marking (50(2)) has a grace period for legacy systems.
why_it_matters: Binding EU disclosure duty for any advisor that speaks as a person or synthesises a real person; draft Commission guidelines pending.
numbers: Fines up to EUR 15M or 3% of global turnover (per CSA and law-firm summaries); 50(2) grace to 2 Dec 2026 for systems already on market.
note: law: disclosure of AI and of deepfakes; in force 2 Aug 2026; secondary sources, read Reg (EU) 2024/1689 | check: Article 50 applies from 2 Aug 2026 (artificialintelligenceact.eu confirms). Not confirmed: the 50(2) grace date 2 Dec 2026 (no source text found; the Nov 2025 Digital Omnibus proposal reportedly set about 2 Feb 2027, check adopted text). Fine ceiling EUR 15M/3% not on the fetched page (Art. 99 not read).
